summary: Explains why RFC 2190, the first RTP payload format for ITU-T H.263 video, should be moved to historic status. It is an informational memo.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo explains why the original RTP payload format for H.263 should become Historic. New implementations are directed to a newer format that can carry the earlier H.263 features as well.

questions: what is the rtp payload format for h.263
why was rfc 2190 moved to historic
subtitle: A recommendation to retire the original RTP payload format for H.263 video.

tldr.problem: RFC 2190 was the first RTP payload format for H.263, while later payload formats could carry the earlier H.263 features too.
tldr.mechanism: The memo recommends moving RFC 2190 to Historic and says new implementations should use RFC 4629 and the H263-1998 and H263-2000 media types.
tldr.outcome: RFC 4628 recommends a transition to the newer format. It says using RFC 4629 instead of RFC 2190 does not change the cited security considerations.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 4628 as Informational and records no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The memo recommends moving RFC 2190 to Historic and using RFC 4629 for new implementations.

sections.title: The H.263 Payload Formats
sections.content:
ITU-T Recommendation H.263 specifies video encoding used by compliant videoconference codecs. RFC 2190 was the first RTP payload format for the 1996 version of H.263.

The 1998 H.263 update added optional features and received a payload format in RFC 2429. RFC 2429 can also carry streams using only the basic version 1 options, although it had said that it did not replace RFC 2190 for existing implementations.
sections.plainLanguage: The original RTP format carried the first H.263 version. Later formats can also carry that version's features, while supporting newer H.263 versions.

sections.title: Recommendation for New Implementations
sections.content:
The memo says all features in the 1996 H.263 version are also part of the 1998 and later versions. RFC 2429 and RFC 4629 can therefore carry new payloads even when they use only the original features.

It recommends moving RFC 2190 to Historic and using RFC 4629, together with the H263-1998 and H263-2000 media types, for new implementations. The recommendation was to take effect at or soon after publication of RFC 4629.
sections.plainLanguage: Because the newer format can carry the original H.263 features too, the memo recommends it for new implementations and retirement of the older format.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The memo points to RFC 4629 for security considerations related to the H.263 RTP payload. It says replacing RFC 2190 with RFC 4629 does not change those considerations because both refer to the same RTP security documents.
sections.plainLanguage: The recommended format change does not alter the cited security considerations. Both payload specifications refer to the same RTP documents.
